scenario: AITA for asking my boyfriend to pick up and drop off my child on weekends which made him suggest a break up? | So for full disclosure my partner works full time and is usually at work from 7am-7pm, and I have a weekend job that requires me to be away from 9am-12pm. We don’t live together but we are local so we are always in and out of each other’s homes. My son decided he wanted to play football on weekends- he’s 12 years old and really excited about it. I was initially going to ask my bf if he could pay for it but I mentioned it to my mum when I went around for a cup of tea and she was strongly expecting me to pay and told me it was my responsibility not my bf’s... even though he’s been in my life 3 years. So I ended up having to pay but in order to afford it I extended my hours at work to 9-5. I asked my bf if he’d be willing to pick up and drop off my son on weekends as obviously if be at work and he looked uncomfortable and said sorry no can’t his dad drop him? I admit I snapped at him and told him that his dad lives in south London whereas we live in north London and his dad doesn’t drive but my boyfriend does. I asked him if he really wanted to be part of this family and if he did he wouldn’t mind doing small stuff like this for me. I suppose his dad COULD take him but what would be a 1 hour + journey for his dad would take 15 minutes for my bf. He got really angry and told me that he was having to work longer hours to support me and my son and that he wanted to use his weekends to go to football games etc as I wasn’t at home anyway. He said that he wanted to chill and relax and that I was forcing things on him way too quick. He then suggested that we break up bc ”I was putting too many responsibilities on him” and I was like.. really? Over a bloody football game? Welcome to the real world love! The little sneak then went over to see my mum and had a heart to heart with her which ended up in HER calling ME and her telling me I am out of line. Who is TA? AITA?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm being too hard on my boyfriend or if he's overreacting. Let me start by laying out the situation as I see it. First, my partner works full-time from 7 am to 7 pm. That's a long day, and I can imagine how exhausting that must be. I have a weekend job that requires me to be away from 9 am to 12 pm. We don't live together, but we're local, so we're always in and out of each other's homes. That seems like a good setup for maintaining a relationship without the constant stress of living together. Now, my son decided he wanted to play football on weekends. He's 12 years old and really excited about it. I was initially going to ask my boyfriend if he could pay for it, but when I mentioned it to my mom during a casual visit, she was strongly expecting me to pay and told me it was my responsibility, not my boyfriend's. That's a bit confusing because he's been in my life for three years, and I thought he was part of the family. So, I ended up having to pay for it myself, but to afford it, I extended my work hours to 9 am to 5 pm. That's a significant increase in my workload. Then, I asked my boyfriend if he could pick up and drop off my son on weekends because, obviously, I'm at work. He looked uncomfortable and said, "Sorry, no can do. This is your dad's responsibility." I snapped at him and told him that his dad lives in South London, whereas we live in North London, and his dad doesn't drive, but my boyfriend does. I asked him if he really wanted to be part of this family and if he did, he wouldn't mind doing small stuff like this for me. I think I might have overreacted here. I mean, it's a small favor, but I was stressed about the financial burden and the increased workload. He got really angry and told me that he has to work longer hours to support me and my son and that he wanted to use his weekends to go to football games, etc., since I'm not home anyway. He said he wanted to chill and relax and that I was forcing things on him way too quickly. Then he suggested that we break up because I was putting too many responsibilities on him. I was shocked and hurt. I thought it was over a bloody football game! I told him, "Welcome to the real world, love!" The little sneak then went to see my mom, and they had a heart-to-heart, which ended up with her calling me and telling me I'm out of line. So, who is in the wrong here? Am I being too demanding, or is he being unreasonable? I need to figure out if I'm AITA (A Guy's Guide to Women) or if he's overreacting. First, let's look at the financial aspect. My mom told me it's my responsibility to pay for my son's football, but I thought my boyfriend, being part of the family, should contribute. I ended up paying for it myself, which required me to work longer hours. That's a lot of pressure. Then, I asked him to help with picking up and dropping off my son on weekends. He refused, saying it's my dad's responsibility. That seems a bit dismissive, especially since he lives closer and can drive. I snapped at him, which probably made things worse. He, in turn, got angry and said he works hard to support us and wants to use his weekends for himself. He suggested breaking up because I'm putting too many responsibilities on him. So, is it fair for me to expect him to help with these responsibilities? Or is he justified in wanting to have his weekends to himself after working long hours? I think both of us have valid points. I'm stressed about the financial burden and the increased workload, and I was hoping for some support from him. He, on the other hand, feels like he's already contributing by working long hours and wants some downtime. Maybe the issue is communication. We didn't discuss these responsibilities beforehand, and I assumed he would be willing to help. He, in turn, felt like I was imposing too much on him without considering his needs. Perhaps we need to sit down and have an open conversation about our expectations and how we can support each other without overburdening either of us. It's important to find a balance where both of our needs are considered. In the end, I think neither of us is entirely right or wrong. It's more about how we communicate and work together to manage our responsibilities and personal time.
